lessons.title: Binary Representation and Bitwise Operators
lessons.concept: Bit manipulation operates directly on binary representations of integers. Common bitwise operators include AND (&), OR (|), XOR (^), NOT (~), left shift (<<), and right shift (>>). These operations are useful for low-level tasks and efficient tricks.
lessons.formula: AND: 1&1=1 else 0. OR: 0|0=0 else 1. XOR: same bits -> 0, different -> 1. Left shift x<<k multiplies by 2^k (for non-overflowing integers). Right shift divides by powers of two (implementation details vary by language/sign).
mistakes: Confusing bitwise operators (&,|,^) with logical operators (&&,||)
Assuming shift behavior is identical across languages for negative numbers
Off-by-one in bit positions (0-indexed from least significant bit is common)

lessons.title: Common Bit Tricks
lessons.concept: Bit tricks solve common tasks efficiently: check if a number is odd/even (n&1), test/set/clear/toggle a specific bit using masks, and check power of two. Masks are integers with particular bit patterns used with bitwise operations.
lessons.formula: Test bit k: (n & (1<<k)) != 0. Set bit k: n | (1<<k). Clear bit k: n & ~(1<<k). Toggle bit k: n ^ (1<<k). Power of two (positive n): (n & (n-1)) == 0.
mistakes: Using wrong mask (1<<k vs k) for bit position
Applying power-of-two test without handling n <= 0 as required by definition

lessons.title: XOR Properties and Applications
lessons.concept: XOR has useful properties: x^x=0, x^0=x, commutative and associative. These enable tasks like finding a unique element when others appear twice, swapping values (conceptually), and toggling bits.
lessons.formula: Properties: a^a=0, a^0=a, a^b=b^a, (a^b)^c=a^(b^c). XOR of all elements where pairs cancel leaves the single unique element.
mistakes: Using XOR uniqueness trick when elements appear other than twice/once pattern assumed
Assuming XOR gives sum or maximum
Operator precedence issues when mixing bitwise and comparison operators

practice.question: What is the result of 5 & 3? (5=0101, 3=0011)
practice.explanation: Bitwise AND keeps 1 only where both bits are 1: 0101 & 0011 = 0001, which is 1.

practice.question: Which expression checks if integer n is odd (common method)?
practice.explanation: The least significant bit is 1 for odd numbers and 0 for even numbers, so n & 1 yields 1 for odd and 0 for even.

options.A: It returns 1 if any bit is 1
options.B: It returns 1 only when both corresponding bits are 1
options.D: It is the same as addition

questions.explanation: Bitwise AND compares corresponding bits and produces 1 only if both bits are 1; otherwise it produces 0.

questions.question: What does x & (x - 1) == 0 test (for x > 0)?

options.B: x is a power of two

questions.explanation: x & (x-1) clears the lowest set bit of x. If the result is 0, x had exactly one set bit - i.e. x is a power of two. (This is the classic Brian Kernighan trick.)

questions.question: How do you flip bit k of an integer x (0-indexed) using OR?
questions.explanation: OR with a mask having only bit k set turns that bit on while leaving others unchanged. AND clears a bit, XOR flips it, and (1 << k) builds the mask.
